senses.sense_definition: To be in a state of boiling or to become boiling hot.

examples.text: The water began to <w>seethe</w> as the temperature reached its peak.
Watch the pot carefully so the soup does not <w>seethe</w> over the sides.

senses.sense_definition: To be in an agitated or angry mental state, often hidden from others.

examples.text: He had to <w>seethe</w> in silence while his boss criticized his work unfairly.
She was <w>seething</w> with frustration after the meeting ended.

senses.sense_definition: To be filled with many people or things moving about actively.

examples.text: The marketplace <w>seethed</w> with tourists and local vendors on Saturday morning.
The city streets <w>seethe</w> with life throughout the entire night.

senses.sense_definition: To cook food by boiling or stewing.

examples.text: The chef instructed the kitchen staff to <w>seethe</w> the meat slowly in the broth.
They <w>seethed</w> the vegetables until they were soft enough to mash.

traits.comment: This usage is largely archaic or literary.
